definition: BRS/Search is a full-text database and information retrieval system.
details: BRS/Search uses a fully inverted indexing system to store, locate, and retrieve unstructured data. It was the search engine that in 1977 powered Bibliographic Retrieval Services (BRS) commercial operations with 20 databases (including the first national commercial availability of MEDLINE); it has changed ownership several times during its development and is currently sold as Livelink ECM Discovery Server by Open Text Corporation.

explainer.lead: BRS/Search is a full-text database system for finding information in collections of unstructured text. It made large bibliographic databases searchable commercially, including providing the first national commercial access to MEDLINE in 1977.

tiers.eli5: Imagine a huge library where every book has an index telling you exactly which pages contain each word. BRS/Search builds that kind of index for a whole collection, so it can quickly find the documents you want without reading every document from start to finish.
tiers.practitioner: BRS/Search stores and retrieves unstructured data through a fully inverted index rather than scanning the text for every query. Its applications included commercial bibliographic retrieval and MEDLINE access; it is now sold as Livelink ECM Discovery Server by Open Text Corporation.
tiers.paperLevel: BRS/Search is a full-text information retrieval system based on a fully inverted index, which associates index terms with their locations in unstructured data. Queries use those associations to locate and retrieve matching records; the supplied description gives no scoring formula or formal retrieval model.

explainer.example: For a collection of medical article records, a query for a term such as "heart" can consult the inverted index, find the records where that term occurs, and retrieve them without scanning every record.

explainer.intuition: Instead of searching every document from beginning to end, build a word-to-location guide first. A search can then jump directly to documents containing the requested text.
howItWorks: Take in unstructured text and database records.
Build a fully inverted index of terms and their locations.
Use the index to locate data matching a query.
Retrieve the matching text or records.
explainer.whyItMatters: It turned large collections of unstructured and bibliographic text into commercially searchable databases. Its 1977 role in BRS and MEDLINE access made it an early notable system in online information retrieval.
misconceptions: It is not just a website search engine; it is a full-text database and retrieval system.
BRS/Search and Bibliographic Retrieval Services are related but not identical: one powered the other's commercial operations.
Its product identity has changed through several ownership changes.
